business_problem: Deutsche Telekom needed a faster and more economical way to plan FTTH fiber routes because excavation cost depends on local surface conditions, tree roots, and restoration work, while manually reviewing large volumes of measurement data would make planning inefficient.
solution_summary: Deutsche Telekom piloted an AI-assisted planning workflow for FTTH roll-out in Bornheim. A measuring vehicle equipped with 360° cameras, laser scanners, and GPS surveys streets and surrounding rights-of-way, capturing detailed environmental and surface data at road level. AI software then processes the measurement data automatically, recognizing, localizing, and classifying route-relevant objects such as trees, street lights, asphalt, paving stones, and cobblestones. A neural network trained with deep learning also distinguishes finer details like pavement size and tree type so the system can estimate excavation effort and restoration impact. After collection, a separate AI stage anonymizes people and vehicles, the prepared dataset is assessed against existing infrastructure to recommend the most economical cable route, and a Deutsche Telekom planner reviews and approves the plan before civil works begin.

solution_components.name: 360° cameras
solution_components.role: Capture street-level environmental imagery from the measuring vehicle for route analysis.

solution_components.name: laser scanners
solution_components.role: Capture detailed physical surface and geometry data along candidate fiber routes.

solution_components.name: GPS technology
solution_components.role: Georeferences the collected measurement data so route conditions can be mapped to exact locations.

solution_components.name: software with artificial intelligence
solution_components.role: Calculates optimal rollout routes and evaluates environmental data for economical planning.

solution_components.name: neural network
solution_components.role: Recognizes and classifies approximately 30 categories in the measurement data for planning decisions.

solution_components.name: specially-trained artificial intelligence
solution_components.role: Makes vehicles and individuals unidentifiable before the planning data is prepared further.

data_flow: A measuring vehicle collects GPS-tagged imagery and laser scan data from the FTTH rollout area, producing detailed surface datasets. AI software evaluates the measurement data, classifies route-relevant objects and surfaces, then applies an anonymization step to hide identifiable people and vehicles. The prepared data is assessed against existing infrastructure to recommend an economical fiber route, which a Deutsche Telekom planner validates before construction.
business_outcome: The pilot speeds up fiber route planning and helps Deutsche Telekom choose more economical rollout paths so it can cover more ground faster and provide broadband lines sooner and more efficiently.
metrics: approximately 5 GB of surface data per kilometer
architecture_clues: Pilot phase ran in Bornheim near Bonn as part of Deutsche Telekom's FTTH project.

evidence_quotes: "Software with artificial intelligence calculates the optimal routes for a faster roll-out"

"A measuring vehicle was sent out in Bornheim (near Bonn) this summer, equipped with 360° cameras and laser scanners as part of Deutsche Telekom's FTTH (Fiber-to-the-home) project. It collected detailed environmental data using GPS technology."
"Depending on the terrain, the vehicle can cover 50 to 80 kilometres per day. All told, it collects approximately 5 GB of surface data per kilometer."
"Fraunhofer IPM has developed software that automatically recognizes, localizes and classifies relevant objects in the measurement data."
"The neural network used for this recognizes a total of approximately 30 different categories through deep learning algorithms."
"Once the data has been collected, a specially-trained artificial intelligence is used to make all vehicles and individuals unidentifiable."
"The existing infrastructure is assessed to determine the optimal route. A Deutsche Telekom planner then double-checks and approves it."
